classification: PRELAUNCH WEB DEPLOYED; RELEASE EXTERNALLY BLOCKED

monitoring.privacy: Low-cardinality operational fields only; never prompts, documents, ciphertext, credentials, full room identifiers, client identifiers, window titles, file paths or user content.

signals.condition: server error rate at or above 2 percent with at least 50 requests
p95 request duration at or above 2000 milliseconds
rate_limited or room_full refusals exceed 10 percent with at least 50 sends

signals.source: authentication, tenant-isolation and secret-access audit events
signals.condition: any confirmed cross-tenant access, credential exposure or forged update acceptance

structuredRecord.privacy: Every field is enumerated at build time, so an unrecognised value is replaced rather than recorded. Latency is a bucket and the provider slot is an ordinal, never a key.
structuredRecord.edgeFunction: One record per request, logged by supabase/functions/ocade-intelligence under the prefix ocade.health.

severities.meaning: Confirmed security, privacy, integrity or widespread data-loss event
Production unavailable, materially degraded or rollback required
Limited degradation with a safe workaround

requiredRecords: decisions, approvals and commands without secret values

dataProtection.provider: Supabase managed backup or point-in-time recovery selected by the owner
dataProtection.restoreTarget: A separately authorized isolated non-production project
requiredRestoreEvidence: backup identifier and UTC timestamp without credentials
restore target destroyed or retained under an approved policy

rehearsal.scope: Schema rebuilt from supabase/migrations into an empty PostgreSQL, rows restored from a backup of a seeded database, then digest, foreign-key, sequence, row-level-security and cross-account checks, and one migration rolled back and re-applied.
rehearsal.note: A local rehearsal against real PostgreSQL. It does not replace the owner-run drill against an isolated Supabase project, which is what requiredRestoreEvidence describes.

rollback.cloudflare: npm run deploy:rollback to a named prior immutable version id, separately approved and health-verified
rollback.edgeFunction: release/OCADE_EDGE_FUNCTION_RELEASES.json records the source of each deployed version; npm run edge:rollback-prove rebuilds it from git and re-hashes it

externalInputsRequired: production health endpoints and alert receivers
custom SMTP credentials and real production email-flow proof
backup retention, offsite-copy and restore-target policy
executed restore drill and incident exercise evidence
